povs.description: Run the real `pr` binary with a multi-tab -S separator (the exact repro from the fix commit: echo a > a; pr -S$'\t\t\t' a -m a). -m merges the two input files into parallel columns, so init_parameters() enters the columns>1 branch, sees a separator starting with '\t', repoints col_sep_string at the 1-byte column_separator while leaving col_sep_length=3, and print_sep_string() reads 2 bytes past the 1-byte global -- ASan global-buffer-overflow.
povs.exploit_path: -S$'\t\t\t' (separator_string: col_sep_length=3, col_sep_string=optarg_S) -> init_parameters columns>1 branch (col_sep_string = column_separator, col_sep_length NOT reset, src/pr.c:1237) -> print_sep_string (s=col_sep_string, l=col_sep_length=3, reads 2 bytes past the 1-byte global, src/pr.c:2224-2241)

povs.description: Same desynchronization with a separator that *starts with* a tab but contains non-tab chars (-S$'\tXX', length 3): init_parameters() only inspects the first byte ('\t'), so col_sep_string is repointed at the 1-byte column_separator while col_sep_length stays 3, and print_sep_string() reads 2 bytes past the global. Guards against a partial fix that special-cases only all-tab separators instead of the length==1 check the official fix uses.
povs.exploit_path: -S$'\tXX' (col_sep_length=3) -> init_parameters (first byte '\t' -> col_sep_string = column_separator, col_sep_length unchanged=3) -> print_sep_string (reads 3 bytes from the 1-byte global, src/pr.c:2225,2241)

command_result.name: gtpov_zip64_truncated_extra_block
command_result.stderr: [gtpov] reproduced: AddressSanitizer crash

covers_alert_paths: zzip/memdisk.c:218 zzip_mem_entry_extra_block(item, ZZIP_EXTRA_zip64) returns a block matched purely on its 2-byte datatype code, with no check that its declared datasize covers struct zzip_extra_zip64
zzip/memdisk.c:219 if (block) bare non-null guard, no size validation
zzip/memdisk.c:224 item->zz_diskstart = ZZIP_GET32(block->z_diskstart) reads 4 bytes 32 bytes into the (possibly truncated) block -- heap-based out-of-bounds read
povs.description: unzzipcat-mem (memdisk API) against a ZIP whose central-directory entry carries a 4-byte extra field encoding a zip64 block header (datatype 0x0001, datasize 0). zzip_mem_entry_extra_block matches it on the bare datatype code and returns it; the override block then reads ZZIP_GET64(block->z_usize) at offset 4 and ZZIP_GET32(block->z_diskstart) at offset 28 from the malloc(ext+2) copy, running well past its end -- a heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 8 reported by AddressSanitizer. Guarded by fix 9e8f867 (blocksize <= datasize + headerlength).
povs.exploit_path: unzzipcat-mem <zip> -> zzip_mem_disk_open -> zzip_disk_open (mmap) -> zzip_mem_disk_load -> zzip_mem_entry_new (memdisk.c:160) -> ext1 = zzip_disk_entry_get_extras(entry) = 4; memcpy 4 bytes into malloc(6) with a 2-byte zero sentinel -> zzip_mem_entry_extra_block(item, ZZIP_EXTRA_zip64) matches datatype 0x0001 (bare non-null guard, memdisk.c:218-219) -> item->zz_usize = ZZIP_GET64(block->z_usize) reads 8 bytes at offset 4 (6..11 past the 6-byte allocation) -> heap-buffer-overflow

covers_alert_paths: zzip/mmapped.c:286 zzip_disk_entry_to_file_header(disk, entry) can return 0 for a crafted disk_entry file-offset; the lookup validates only the offset range, not the candidate header's magic-number field
zzip/memdisk.c:174 struct zzip_file_header *header = zzip_disk_entry_to_file_header(disk, entry) return value stored with no null check
zzip/memdisk.c:182 item->zz_data = zzip_file_header_to_data(header) header dereferenced unconditionally -- heap-based out-of-bounds read once a failed lookup is walked
povs.description: unzzipcat-mem (memdisk API) against a ZIP whose single central-directory entry's local-header offset field points past the end of the file. zzip_disk_entry_to_file_header (zzip/mmapped.c:286) validates only the offset range, returns 0 for the out-of-range offset, and zzip_mem_entry_new stores the result with no null check -- zzip_file_header_to_data(header) at memdisk.c:182 then dereferences the unguarded header, crashing on a near-null address (SEGV).
povs.exploit_path: unzzipcat-mem <zip> -> zzip_mem_disk_open -> zzip_disk_open (mmap) -> zzip_mem_disk_load -> zzip_mem_entry_new (memdisk.c:160) -> header = zzip_disk_entry_to_file_header(disk, entry) returns 0 because file_header = buffer + offset >= endbuf (mmapped.c:286) -> item->zz_comment / item->zz_name resolved from the central dir itself (no header deref) -> item->zz_data = zzip_file_header_to_data(header) reads header->z_namlen / header->z_extras at address ~0x16 (memdisk.c:182) -> SEGV on the unguarded failed lookup

covers_alert_paths: zzip/mmapped.c:286 zzip_disk_entry_to_file_header(disk, entry) validates only the offset range, not the candidate header's magic-number field -- an in-range offset pointing at non-local-header bytes returns a bogus non-null header
zzip/memdisk.c:182 item->zz_data = zzip_file_header_to_data(header) header dereferenced unconditionally -- the bogus header's z_namlen/z_extras are read from arbitrary bytes
povs.description: unzzipcat-mem (memdisk API) against a ZIP whose central-directory entry's local-header offset points at an IN-range location that is not a local file header (magic != PK\003\004) and whose bytes at +28 are 0xFFFF. zzip_disk_entry_to_file_header returns the bogus non-null header (the range check passes), and zzip_mem_entry_new reads z_extras = 0xFFFF from it and memcpy(mem, ptr2, 0xFFFF) reads far past the file. This exercises the magic-check half of the fix (33d6e9c): the null check alone (64e745f) does NOT block it.
povs.exploit_path: unzzipcat-mem <zip> -> zzip_mem_disk_open -> zzip_mem_disk_load -> zzip_mem_entry_new (memdisk.c:160) -> header = zzip_disk_entry_to_file_header(disk, entry) returns a non-null pointer into disk->buffer at an offset whose magic != ZZIP_FILE_HEADER_MAGIC (mmapped.c:286, no magic check pre-fix) -> zzip_file_header_get_extras(header) reads 0xFFFF from the bogus header -> memcpy(mem, zzip_file_header_to_extras(header), 0xFFFF) reads far past endbuf -> OOB read

povs.exploit_path: imginfo -> image format decoder parses width/height/prec from the file header into cmptparms -> jas_image_create() -> rawsize += cmptparm->width * cmptparm->height * (cmptparm->prec + 7) / 8 (no overflow check)

covers_alert_paths: read_and_discard_scanlines() (jdapistd.c) unconditionally dereferences cinfo->cconvert->color_convert while installing its dummy converter -- but under merged upsampling cinfo->cconvert is NULL, so the jpeg_skip_scanlines discard path itself NULL-derefs before any pixel is written
the merged-upsampling skip path is a distinct sink from every quantizer sink and is closed only by the cconvert NULL-guard added in commit 398c1e9
povs.description: Merged (non-fancy) upsampling with color quantization DISABLED (quantize_colors=FALSE, do_fancy_upsampling=FALSE, RGB output). With merged 4:2:0 upsampling the decoder installs no separate color converter (cinfo->cconvert is NULL), so when jpeg_skip_scanlines() routes the discard through read_and_discard_scanlines(), that function NULL-derefs cinfo->cconvert->color_convert. This path carries NO quantizer, so the noop_quantize fix (5bc43c7) alone does not close it -- it is closed by the cconvert NULL-guard in commit 398c1e9. NOTE: on this dataset revision the observed crash site is read_and_discard_scanlines() (jdapistd.c) via the NULL cconvert, not merged_2v_upsample (jdmerge.c:282); the alert's merged_2v_upsample line and this cconvert deref are the same merged-upsampling skip fault, closed by the same commit.

povs.description: swftophp against getString_const8.swf: a DoAction block with a 1-entry CONSTANTPOOL followed by PUSH [CONSTANT8=255] + CALLFUNCTION. decompileCALLFUNCTION renders the argument list via newVar_N -> getString(pop()), which indexes pool[255] although sact->Count==1 -- an OOB/stale pointer read (heap-use-after-free/heap-buffer-overflow under ASan) at util/decompile.c:349.

covers_alert_paths: TIFFGetFieldDefaulted(in, TIFFTAG_SAMPLESPERPIXEL, &spp): untrusted SamplesPerPixel tag read from the input file, no upper-bound check (tools/tiffcrop.c:5755)
if ((bps == 0) || (spp == 0)) return (-1): the only validation spp ever receives -- a zero check, never an upper bound (tools/tiffcrop.c:5932)
readSeparateStripsIntoBuffer(in, read_buff, length, width, spp, dump) at tools/tiffcrop.c:6060 passes the unbounded spp into combineSeparateSamples16bits at :4811

for (s = 0; s < spp; s++) { src = in[s] + src_offset + src_byte; ... } -- combineSeparateSamples16bits (tools/tiffcrop.c:3840) iterates over the caller's 8-slot srcbuffs[] array with the raw spp=9, reading in[8] out of bounds (READ of size 8) and dereferencing the garbage pointer
povs.description: tiffcrop against a strip-based PLANARCONFIG=separate TIFF (1_strip_16bits.tif: 3x16, BitsPerSample=3, SamplesPerPixel=9). loadImage reads spp=9 unchecked, readSeparateStripsIntoBuffer's own read loop bounds at MAX_SAMPLES=8 and fills srcbuffs[8], then the bps%8!=0 dispatch (shift_width=2) calls combineSeparateSamples16bits (tiffcrop.c:3840) whose `for (s = 0; s < spp; s++)` merge loop indexes in[8] -- an AddressSanitizer stack-buffer-overflow READ of the srcbuffs[] pointer array. With the official fix bounding that loop by (s < MAX_SAMPLES) the merge skips the 9th plane; because the 3-bit samples leave >=1 padding byte at the end of each 2-byte row, the function's 2-byte-per-sample source reads stay in-bounds and tiffcrop completes cleanly (blocked).
povs.exploit_path: tiffcrop in.tif out.tif -> loadImage -> TIFFGetFieldDefaulted(SAMPLESPERPIXEL)=9 (no upper bound) -> readSeparateStripsIntoBuffer -> combineSeparateSamples16bits -> `for (s = 0; s < spp; s++)` reads in[8] past the MAX_SAMPLES-sized srcbuffs[] stack array -> stack-buffer-overflow

povs.description: Same strip-based separate-planar shape with BitsPerSample=28 (3_strip_32bits.tif: 64x16, spp=9): shift_width=5 routes to combineSeparateSamples32bits (tiffcrop.c:4076), whose unbounded `for (s = 0; s < spp; s++)` merge loop with spp=9 reads in[8] past the srcbuffs[MAX_SAMPLES] stack array and dereferences the garbage pointer. With the fix, the loop stops at s<8 and the 4-byte source reads exactly span the 28-bit samples (row gap of 4 bytes), so tiffcrop completes cleanly (blocked). BitsPerSample=28 is chosen deliberately: a multiple-of-8 bps (8/16/32) routes to the already-bounded combineSeparateSamplesBytes path instead.

command_result.name: gtpov_sepstrips_rowsperstrip_uint32_wrap
command_result.stderr: [gtpov] reproduced: unsigned-integer-overflow in rowstripsize multiply

covers_alert_paths: (void) TIFFGetFieldDefaulted(out, TIFFTAG_ROWSPERSTRIP, &rowsperstrip) : untrusted TIFF tag value read with no upper-bound check (tools/tiffcrop.c:1164)
(void) TIFFGetField(out, TIFFTAG_BITSPERSAMPLE, &bps) : untrusted TIFF tag value feeding bytes_per_sample = (bps + 7) / 8 on the next line, also unchecked (tools/tiffcrop.c:1165)
rowstripsize = rowsperstrip * bytes_per_sample * (width + 1) : plain uint32 multiplication of three attacker-influenced values, no overflow guard (tools/tiffcrop.c:1168)

obuf = _TIFFmalloc(rowstripsize) : the wrapped, undersized value sizes the heap allocation that the row-copy loop below then reads/writes past -- CWE-190 root cause producing a CWE-125 out-of-bounds read (tools/tiffcrop.c:1170)
povs.description: tiffcrop (no flags) against a crafted 15x1 8-bit JPEG TIFF with PlanarConfiguration=SEPARATE and RowsPerStrip=0x80000000. tiffcrop copies the input's huge RowsPerStrip onto the output image (the clamp to the image length only applies when compression != JPEG), so writeBufferToSeparateStrips computes rowstripsize = 2^31 * 1 * (15+1) = 2^35, which wraps a uint32 to 0; _TIFFmalloc(0) sizes obuf and the row-copy loop (memset 0 bytes, extractContigSamplesToBuffer writing the strip, TIFFWriteEncodedStrip) works against an effectively empty buffer -- the CWE-190 wrap behind the CWE-125 OOB read. clang -fsanitize=unsigned-integer-overflow (the dataset build's sanitizer) reports 'runtime error: unsigned integer overflow: 2147483648 * 16' at tiffcrop.c:1168 before the corruption. The official fix's guard rejects the same input with 'Error, uint32 overflow when computing rowsperstrip * bytes_per_sample * (width + 1)' and no UBSan report.
povs.exploit_path: sep_strip.tif tags (RowsPerStrip=2^31, BitsPerSample=8, ImageWidth=15, PlanarConfiguration=SEPARATE, Compression=JPEG) -> TIFFOpen/loadImage (reads tags, malloc(stripsize) succeeds - 64-bit tsize_t) -> writeCroppedImage copies RowsPerStrip to the output TIFF (unclamped: JPEG) -> writeBufferToSeparateStrips (tools/tiffcrop.c:1168) -> rowstripsize = 2^31 * 1 * 16 wraps to 0 -> _TIFFmalloc(0) + row-copy loop OOB write/read (CWE-190 -> CWE-125)

covers_alert_paths: CopyField(TIFFTAG_BITSPERSAMPLE, bitspersample) reads the attacker-controlled 1-bit value at tools/tiffcp.c:602
pickCopyFunc() selects cpContig2SeparateByRow from planar config only (its bitspersample guard requires samplesperpixel>1, which a 1-sample image avoids) at tools/tiffcp.c:813

cpContig2SeparateByRow `*outp++ = *inp; inp += spp;` for imagewidth iterations into inbuf/outbuf sized by TIFFScanlineSize() (ceil(width/8) bytes for 1-bit) -- OOB heap read AND write at tools/tiffcp.c:1090
povs.description: tiffcp -p separate against a 1-bit, 1-sample, planar=contig TIFF (1.tif) routes to cpContig2SeparateByRow (tools/tiffcp.c:1090), whose per-row copy loop treats each sample as 1 byte for `imagewidth` iterations while the row buffers are sized by TIFFScanlineSize() (ceil(imagewidth/8) bytes for BitsPerSample=1), producing a heap-buffer-overflow read (inp) and write (outp) under AddressSanitizer.
povs.exploit_path: tiffcp -p separate -> TIFFOpen reads BitsPerSample=1 via CopyField -> pickCopyFunc (spp=1 avoids the only bitspersample guard) -> cpContig2SeparateByRow -> `for (n=imagewidth; n--;) { *outp++ = *inp; inp += spp; }` walks inp/outp past the ceil(width/8)-byte TIFFScanlineSize() buffers

covers_alert_paths: CopyField(TIFFTAG_BITSPERSAMPLE, bitspersample) reads the attacker-controlled 1-bit value at tools/tiffcp.c:602
pickCopyFunc() selects cpSeparate2ContigByRow from planar config only (its bitspersample guard requires samplesperpixel>1, which a 1-sample image avoids) at tools/tiffcp.c:813

cpSeparate2ContigByRow `*outp = *inp++; outp += spp;` for imagewidth iterations into inbuf/outbuf sized by TIFFScanlineSize() (ceil(width/8) bytes for 1-bit) -- OOB heap read AND write at tools/tiffcp.c:1143
povs.description: tiffcp -p contig against a 1-bit, 1-sample, planar=separate TIFF (2.tif) routes to cpSeparate2ContigByRow (tools/tiffcp.c:1143), whose per-row merge loop treats each sample as 1 byte for `imagewidth` iterations while the row buffers are sized by TIFFScanlineSize() (ceil(imagewidth/8) bytes for BitsPerSample=1), producing a heap-buffer-overflow read (inp) and write (outp) under AddressSanitizer.
povs.exploit_path: tiffcp -p contig -> TIFFOpen reads BitsPerSample=1 via CopyField -> pickCopyFunc (spp=1 avoids the only bitspersample guard) -> cpSeparate2ContigByRow -> `for (n=imagewidth; n--;) { *outp = *inp++; outp += spp; }` walks inp/outp past the ceil(width/8)-byte TIFFScanlineSize() buffers

covers_alert_paths: OJPEGDecode() unguarded dispatch into OJPEGDecodeRaw() after a failed OJPEGPreDecode (libtiff/tif_ojpeg.c:785) -> 'if (cc%sp->bytes_per_line!=0)' integer divide-by-zero (libtiff/tif_ojpeg.c:816)
povs.description: Drives the identical OJPEGDecodeRaw 'cc % bytes_per_line' divide-by-zero (tif_ojpeg.c:816) through the libtiff PUBLIC API instead of the tiffmedian tool. A ~20-line C driver (povs/ojpeg_scanline.c) compiled against the static libtiff.a does TIFFOpen -> TIFFReadScanline(t,buf,0,0) (fails in OJPEGReadHeaderInfo, returns -1) -> TIFFReadScanline(t,buf,0,0) AGAIN. On the second read of row 0, strip==tif->tif_curstrip (TIFFStartStrip set it before the first read's predecode failed), so TIFFSeek skips the refill/predecode and OJPEGDecode runs on the zero-initialized codec state (bytes_per_line==0) -> 3 % 0. With the official decoder_ok fix, OJPEGDecode early-exits ('Cannot decode: decoder not correctly initialized') on the second read and no division runs. Decouples the ground-truth coverage from the specific behaviour of any one CLI tool.
povs.exploit_path: crafted BigTIFF OJPEG TIFF (poc_00083, 1x1) -> TIFFOpen -> TIFFReadScanline(row 0) #1: TIFFSeek/TIFFStartStrip set tif_curstrip=0, OJPEGPreDecode fails in OJPEGReadHeaderInfo (tif_ojpeg.c:674), read returns -1 -> TIFFReadScanline(row 0) #2: strip==tif_curstrip so TIFFSeek skips predecode -> tif_decoderow=OJPEGDecode (tif_ojpeg.c:785) -> OJPEGDecodeRaw 'if (cc%sp->bytes_per_line!=0)' (tif_ojpeg.c:816) divides by the zero-initialized bytes_per_line
